answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can earn reputation or influence payouts. A newcomer may tell a fable or use the name marble, but creating thousands of identities still requires thousands of independently funded bonds; splitting one stake across them makes each claim less influential. If an account is caught coordinating fraud, its bond is slashed, so the attacker pays real capital and risks losing it, even in an ocean of cheap identities.
